evidence.claim: Zebra describes itself as a provider of hardware, software, automation solutions and services for frontline workflows, including retail; it identifies leadership positions in rugged mobile computing, barcode scanning, RFID readers, thermal printing, and retail task-management software.

memory_update.text: ZBRA is the reference anchor for retail auto-ID hardware/software: barcode, RFID readers, mobile computers, printers, and inventory visibility.
AVY is the reference anchor for RFID/intelligent labels and consumable tag exposure; verify Intelligent Labels mix and raw-material margin sensitivity.
PI is a mid-cap underfollowed pure-play candidate for RAIN RFID chips/readers and item-level retail tagging expansion.

SPSC is an underfollowed software-network candidate for retailer compliance infrastructure, EDI, fulfillment, trading-partner onboarding, and chargeback workflows; RFID-specific exposure remains to be verified.

The RFID/labeling chokepoint should be split in later layers into consumables/inlays, silicon/readers, printers/scanners/mobile devices, service bureaus/certification, middleware/EDI/compliance, and retailer/supplier demand anchors.

Need a later pass for smaller public label/service-bureau names and distributors; many strongest Walmart RFID compliance service providers appear private, so public-market mapping may rely on larger listed suppliers or indirect software networks.

summary: Expanded the RFID / barcode / labeling / retailer-compliance node into a two-lane universe. Reference lane includes larger auto-ID and intelligent-label leaders that anchor the category. Underfollowed lane prioritizes purer or more obscure second-order beneficiaries: RAIN RFID silicon / readers and retail trading-partner compliance networks. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
